title: One toolkit. Three flowers.
summary: Compose petals, leaves and a folded lip from shared surfaces, then animate their opening.
prompt: In Polynite, compose a pink lotus, a daisy and an orchid from editable assembly recipes, using shared surface, repeat and motion operators. Give their petals a smooth four-second opening loop. Keep each flower independently editable. Expose petal count, shape, colour and opening controls. Use the linked example as a starting point, then invent your own variation.
try: Set animate to 0 and vary opening from 0 to 1.
Change petal count and profile to invent a fourth flower.
Enable animate and compare the closed and open poses.
steps: Shape one petal with a reusable curved surface.
Repeat it around a centre; arrange additional layers in the recipe.
Add leaves and a central piece, then articulate the petals with motion.
settings: Scene settings > Living architecture > select lotus, daisy or orchid > Parameters: shape / profile / materials / animation. Set animate = 1, duration = 4, then Play.
limits: Stylised flowers. This is a shared surface-and-articulation recipe, not botanical simulation. The film was recorded on 15 October; regression checks were repeated on 16 October.
